President-elect Nicolas Maduro has signed a new constitution to effectively shrink power to Venezuela's former opposition government.

The law, which is set to go law on Thursday, comes just days after Mr Maduro faces his own transition to power.

The measure marks the most significant transformation of the former opposition leader since it started in last year's elections.

This will see him locked in to months of deepening economic turmoil, with an economic slowdown and increasing gridlock.

The new government is likely to be opposed by the opposition Transparency and Socialism Congress (NED), whom Mr Maduro has ruled largely over the past several years.

NED leader Ruspe Capriles has said that the election is presenting a "threshold gamble on Venezuela".

Ms Capailes was expected to deliver the approval to Mr Maduro, where he has the opportunity to talk about the "growing problems" of his country, including debt, fragmentation and inflation.
